bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Australia Salary Calculator

If you’re looking to convert your hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, or weekly pay, the **Australia Salary Calculator** on this site gives you a clear estimate based on the standard 38-hour week. Whether you’re comparing a salary offer, budgeting for a new job, or checking your current pay, this tool uses the latest Fair Work and Australian Taxation Office figures to help you see the full picture.

### How to Calculate Annual Salary from Hourly Rate

The core formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross pay is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,267.44 (rounded)

This is the figure before tax, Medicare, and super. The calculator assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. If your hours differ, you can adjust the weekly hours in the calculator to match your situation.

### The National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

However, most employees are covered by an award – a specific industry or occupation pay standard. Award rates are typically higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026 – well above the minimum. The **Australia Salary Calculator** does not assume a particular award; it simply uses the rate you enter. If you are on an award, check your classification and enter the correct base rate. The calculator’s casual loading checkbox adds 25% on top of that base rate, as per the Fair Work Ombudsman’s definition.

It’s important to note that the figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics are averages across industries and states, not medians for a specific job. Your actual pay may differ based on your award, experience, and location.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the National Minimum Wage example:

Weekly pay: $1,004.90
Fortnightly pay: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80

The **Australia Salary Calculator** shows both weekly and fortnightly figures, making it easy to align with your pay cycle. This is especially useful for budgeting rent, bills, and savings.

### Tax and Medicare

The calculator estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation. The tax-free threshold is assumed, and no deductions for HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging are included. For a precise tax estimate, consult the Australian Taxation Office or a tax professional.

### Superannuation

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% for 2026–27, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual ordinary earnings exceed that cap, super is only paid on the first $270,830.

The **Australia Salary Calculator** shows super as an additional amount, not included in your gross annual salary. For example, on a $52,267 annual salary, the super estimate would be $6,272 (12% of $52,267), assuming no cap applies. Your total remuneration package includes both salary and super.

### Using the Calculator

To use the **Australia Salary Calculator**, go to [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate – the rate before any casual loading. If you are a casual employee, tick the checkbox to add 25% casual loading. The calculator will then show your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, along with estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember, the calculator is an estimate; your actual pay may vary due to award conditions, overtime, or salary packaging.

For more details on specific topics, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) guide, [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) explanation, or [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
